messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: Potential problem in poisson_rng
parts:
Hi,

The code
generated quantities {
    int <lower = 0> y_rep [N];

    for (i in 1 : N) {
        y_rep [i] <- poisson_rng (gamma_rng (shape [lot [i]], shape [lot [i]] / exp (mu [i])));
    }
}
gives a message
Error : Invalid value of y_rep: Error in function model20b82acf176a_nb3_namespace::write_array(i): y_rep[k0__] is -2147483648, but must be greater than 0

I wonder if this is by design.

Also, there is something going with neg_binomial_rng.

The example below shows that poison_rng(gamma_rng) is not equivalent to neg_binomial_rng. 
mu <- 2
shape <- 4
fit <- stan (model_code = '
    data {
        real shape;
        real mu;
    }
    parameters {
        real any; // just a dummy to make this compile
    }
    model {
        any ~ normal (0, 1);
    }
    generated quantities {
        real y_correct [1000];
        real y_incorrect [1000];

        for (i in 1 : 1000) {
            y_correct [i] <- poisson_rng (gamma_rng (shape, shape / mu));
        }

        for (i in 1 : 1000) {
            y_incorrect [i] <- neg_binomial_rng (shape, shape / mu);
        }
    }', data = list (shape = shape, mu = mu))

mfit <- as.matrix (fit)
correct_sample <- mfit [, grep ("y_correct", colnames (mfit))]
incorrect_sample <- mfit [, grep ("y_incorrect", colnames (mfit))]

set.seed (123)
r_test <- rnbinom (1000, mu = mu, size = shape)
set.seed (123)
r_test1 <- rnbinom (1000, prob = (shape / mu) / ((shape / mu) + 1),
    size = shape)
plot (density (correct_sample [1, ]))
lines (density (incorrect_sample [1, ]), col = "red")
lines (density (r_test), col = "green")
lines (density (r_test1), col = "blue")

Thanks for any help,
Linas

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Potential problem in poisson_rng
parts:
Thanks for the careful report.

It looks like two issues.

1. Negative results from poisson_rng are not by design.
I'm wondering if it's an overflow issue. Any idea what the mean
fed into poisson_rng is that's causing the problem?

We should probably set up the RNGs to check for overflow
and throw exceptions. There's no infinite value for ints the
way there is for real values.

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/625

Do you happen to have a reproducible seed and values for lot and mu that
cause the problem? Ideally, just a simpler case not involving an array.


2. The RNG issue, which assuming the parameterizations are all correct,
would be a separate bug. I know there's been ongoing work on negative_binomial,
but all the parameterizations of that (and gamma) still make my head hurt.

I created an issue to investigate:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/626

- Bob

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Potential problem in poisson_rng
parts:
The _rng functions use Stan’s internal RNG so they should be completely reproducible
given the same seed.  You can also split out the generation of the poisson_rng, saving
the intermediate gamma_rng as a generated quantity.  Or you can just use the print
function.
